It shares a common root with kxaú /kʀau/, from the half-built protolanguage, which used sound changes to differentiate the "aspect of something" versus the actual thing, much like the active/passive system in the current language. Hello. As the title says I'm fairly new to being a DM and I'd like to find some quality resources for enhancing the game for my players. I've been rolling dice as a character for just about 20 years now and recently I've started being DM semi-regularly, I know the rules for most of the systems I play and I don't have any problem making stat blocks for the various baddies the group fights but flavor text and mood setting are two areas I find myself lacking.

Any recommended reading or podcasts y'all have would be greatly appreciated. Thanks for taking the time to read this and I hope you have a nice day.
Relatively new to being a DM, looking for resources that can help.

Something I've found to really help set the mood is background ambiance. Recently I've been using this site. It's pretty amazing. There's little to no music, it's just sounds and such that fit certain themes, so you and your players don't have to talk over music. It really helps keep people "in-game" while playing.

Used to only DM for years, always preferred it over being a character for some reason. Couple of things that really help out, first is pretty obvious and that's reading novels. Descriptive word usage, environment details, and even little things you wouldn't think about, "As you enter the room a lone rat scurrying into a crevice rears up on it's hind legs." Rather stupid but you get the point, It's all about the amount of terminology and different words you are exposed to that will increase your vocabulary. During the day when you have time sitting in an office or a room mentally describe the situation to yourself and add some flare to it. Picture actions taking place in your setting and how you would describe it.

Writing also helps a lot but can be more frustrating. Simple short stories that involve a single room is a fun technique. How much description and action can take place in a single room? Amazingly a lot but it's all in the eyes of the narrator to make it fun and exciting (just like a DM).

Last word of advice would be to do 1 on 1 DMing. This was probably the most useful thing for me. When we couldn't get a big group together I would do back stories and character development with a friend before the game. This really gets the members into their character and helps flesh out who they want to be which just adds more to the enjoyment and purpose of these games. Even if it's not a character they are going to use again it's still fun and great practice because you are focused on painting a picture for that one person instead of wrangling a group of 4 battling to the death with rolls and movements.
Thanks for the suggestions, I appreciate them.
